Hi Ellie — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our call)
- Primary use case: real-time insights and short summaries surfaced in the BrightMetrics UI (user-facing).
- Traffic profile: a mix of hot (interactive) routes + large background batch jobs (ingest/embeddings).
- Desired latency: ideally <= 300ms p95 on interactive routes; streaming would be a plus for perceived responsiveness.
- Budget: you mentioned a monthly envelope that could flex depending on unit economics; you asked for target $/1M tokens to model internal ROI.

What I captured as our deliverables:
1) Cost sketch for three serving options (hosted standard, hosted performance, dedicated/reserved) with example unit economics ($/1M tokens) and expected p95.
2) Suggested hybrid routing: streaming for hot routes, small-batch + caching for background jobs.
3) Draft Mutual Action Plan (attached) with timelines for a trial and PO.

Quick questions to validate before I send numbers: 
- Can you confirm the expected monthly token volume range for month 1 and steady-state? (ballpark is fine: e.g., 50M-200M/month)
- Do you have an internal target for $/1M tokens that would make this attractive? (gives us an anchor for pricing scenarios)
- Is compliance around audit logs and KMS mandatory for go/no-go, or can that be scoped after an initial trial?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send a short cost/latency comparison doc (one-pager) and a MAP by EOD.
- Technical call with your infra lead and our infra engineer (Sean) — can we schedule next Tue/Wed?
- If the economics look good, we’ll spin up a short trial with telemetry to measure real p95 and token usage against your routes.

Attaching a quick unit-econ schematic and the MAP for your review.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items below: 

Volumes (ballpark)
- Month 1 (pilot): 50M - 80M tokens (mostly interactive, small prompt sizes).
- Steady-state (Q3/Q4): 180M - 320M tokens/month (spikey: weekday peak ~3x baseline).

Budget and unit target
- We’re modeling a target of around $70 - $90 per 1M tokens to hit our cost targets for the product (this is flexible if latency is significantly better).
- Monthly procurement budget we could allocate for a pilot: ~$8k-$15k. For production we can go up to $30k/mo if unit economics align.

Latency/SLOs
- Target for user-facing routes: p95 <= 300ms; p99 ideally < 600ms but not a hard blocker initially.
- Streaming is preferred for the most interactive screens (progressive synth) but not required across everything.

Compliance
- Audit logs + KMS required before a full production rollout; for the pilot we can accept a limited evidence set if you can provide network isolation options.

Next steps
- Please send the cost comparison + MAP. Also include sample committed spend thresholds to hit the $70/1M band you mentioned on the call.
- Wed/Thu next week works for a technical deep-dive (Sean and our infra lead, Marco).

—Ellie

Thanks Ellie — good anchors. Attached is a concise cost/latency comparison and a draft MAP. Key notes below (summary so you can forward to finance/infra):

High-level server options (hosted)
1) Hosted - Standard (cost-optimized)
   - Typical p95: ~350-450ms (depends on prompt size & cache hit rate)
   - $/1M tokens (estimate): ~$95/1M tokens (no commit)
   - Best for background jobs + non-critical routes
2) Hosted - Performance (low-latency)
   - Typical p95: ~140-220ms (streaming enabled, faster kernels)
   - $/1M tokens (estimate): ~$160/1M tokens (no commit)
3) Dedicated / Reserved (monthly commit)
   - Typical p95: configurable; we can target <=250ms p95 with appropriate instance sizing + reserved NVMe cache
   - $/1M tokens (estimate): ~$70/1M tokens (with a 6–12 month commit; depends on volume band)

Hybrid suggestion
- Route interactive UI traffic to the Performance tier (or a small dedicated pool) and route heavy batch/ingest to Standard with large-batch windows and caching. This typically yields ~20–40% cost reduction vs sending everything to Performance while keeping UX latency tight.

Unit economics (example scenarios)
- Pilot (50M tokens): Hosted Performance => ~$8,000 (est); Hosted Standard => ~$4,750 (est); Dedicated unlikely to be cost-effective at pilot scale without commit.
- Steady-state (250M tokens): Dedicated (commit) => ~$17,500 (est at $70/1M); Hosted Performance => ~$40,000 (est at $160/1M); Hosted Standard => ~$23,750 (est at $95/1M).

What it takes to reach ~$70/1M band
- Typically we reach that range with a 6–12 month reserved capacity commitment and a volume band in the ~150M+/mo range, or with a blended contract that includes burst credits. We can provide a modeled contract appendix showing tiers and exact bands for your CFO.

Tradeoffs and tuning knobs
- Batching: Aggressive batching reduces $/token but increases tail latency. For interactive routes we use small-batch windows and streaming to preserve p95.
- KV/prefix caching: Cache hot prompts to reduce token count for repeated prompts (huge lever for chat-like UX).
- Quantization & model variants: We can suggest quantized variants for background routes to cut cost ~25–40% with minimal quality loss.

Attachments included: redwood-unit-econ-chart.png, mutual-action-plan-BrightMetrics-v1.pdf, SLA-draft-BM.docx

- I’ll prepare a short contract appendix showing commit tiers required to hit $70/1M.

If that sounds good I’ll get the scheduler invite out now.

Best —
Karthik
